examShortTricks: Trick 1: Dalton's postulates that later FAILED are the exam favourites — atoms divisible (sub-atomic particles), same element can have different masses (isotopes), atoms can be destroyed (nuclear reactions). Quote these three for a 'limitations' question.
Trick 2: Law of multiple proportions is the ONLY law Dalton's theory explained directly — link one postulate (atoms combine in fixed whole-number ratios) to that law in 1 line.
Trick 3: 2-mark question pattern: 'state any two postulates' — always pair one valid postulate with one limitation to show depth.
keyPoints: Matter is made of indivisible atoms (later disproved by electron, proton, neutron).
Atoms of the same element are identical in mass and properties — isotopes disproved this.
Atoms combine in simple whole-number ratios — explains the law of multiple proportions.
Atoms are neither created nor destroyed in chemical reactions — basis of the law of conservation of mass.
practiceQuestions: Q. State any two postulates of Dalton's atomic theory and give one limitation of each. (2 marks) — Postulate: indivisible atoms; limitation: electron/proton/neutron exist. Postulate: identical atoms of an element; limitation: isotopes (1H, 2H, 3H) differ in mass.
Q. Which law of chemical combination is directly explained by Dalton's theory? (1 mark) — Law of multiple proportions.
